These resources are curated for staying up-to-date with the latest
developments in climate change, covering the scientific, political, and
economic landscapes.

## Websites

- [**Yale Climate Connections**](https://yaleclimateconnections.org/) A
  nonpartisan news service helping the public understand the reality of
  climate change and actionable solutions. Staffed by professional
  journalists, meteorologists, and producers, this initiative is part of
  the Yale Center for Environmental Communication at the Yale School of
  the Environment.

- [**Project Drawdown**](https://drawdown.org) An independent nonprofit
  organization driving bold, science-based climate action to help the
  world reach "drawdown"—the point in the future when levels of
  greenhouse gases in the atmosphere stop climbing and start to steadily
  decline.

- [**Season of Creation**](https://seasonofcreation.org/) Activities and
  resources to celebrate the Season of Creation are supported by an
  ecumenical steering committee and a coalition of partners from around
  the world.

## Newsletters and Blogs

- [**Katharine Hayhoe**](https://katharinehayhoe.com/) Dr. Katharine
  Hayhoe is the Chief Scientist for The Nature Conservancy and a
  professor at Texas Tech University. Her work focuses on assessing the
  regional impacts of climate change. She is also the co-author of *A
  Climate for Change: Global Warming Facts for Faith-Based Decisions*, a
  book designed to untangle complex science for faith-based audiences.

- [**The Climate Brink**](https://substack.com/@theclimatebrink) **–
  Andrew Dessler** A newsletter by Dr. Andrew Dessler, a professor of
  Atmospheric Sciences at Texas A&M University. He is the author of the
  textbook *Introduction to Modern Climate Change* and provides deep,
  expert insights into current climate policy and science.

- [**Climate Uncensored**](https://jimehansen.substack.com/) **– Dr.
  James E. Hansen** Dr. Hansen is the Director of Climate Science,
  Awareness and Solutions at Columbia University and the former Director
  of the NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies. Known for his
  pioneering role in climate science advocacy, his newsletter offers
  direct and often urgent perspectives on the climate crisis.

- [**Climate Cafe**](https://climatecafe.substack.com/) A collaborative
  effort by natural and social scientists. This newsletter focuses on
  the intersection of climate analysis and communication, aiming to keep
  the urgency of the crisis and its potential solutions at the forefront
  of public discourse.

- [**Heatmap News**](https://heatmap.news/) Heatmap News is climate news
  for the real world. We tell the inside story of the race to fix the
  planet, with deep reporting on emerging decarbonization trends, like
  electric vehicles, clean hydrogen, and carbon capture, in addition to
  climate change and its impact on our economy, politics, and society.

## Other Dioceses

- [**Diocese of Long Island**](https://www.dioceseli.org/creationcare)
  The Creation Care Community of the Diocese of Long Island (CCCDLI)
  consists of individuals who share a care for creation and a commitment
  to finding ways, as Christians, to address environmental degradation
  and climate change.

- [**Diocese of Northern
  California**](https://www.norcalepiscopal.org/site/commission-on-the-environment/#tab-id-1)
  The primary focus of the Commission is to provide guidance and
  resources to congregations in the Diocese to reduce their carbon
  footprint in order to achieve carbon neutrality by 2030.

- [**Diocese of Chicago**](https://episcopalchicago.org/eco-diochicago/)
  Eco DioChicago is the Diocese of Chicago’s creation care committee,
  formed in August 2024 as a working group and made a committee at the
  2025 Annual Diocesan Convention. Our group is committed to promoting
  care for creation and environmental justice as priorities for our
  diocese and parishes through growing connections, providing useful and
  encouraging resources, and advocating for our mission in the diocese
  and our parishes.

- [**Diocese of
  Washington**](https://edow.org/ministries-programs/equity-and-justice/creation-care/)
  The Episcopal Church and the Diocese of Washington are committed to
  promoting respectful care of God’s creation, and particularly to
  working against climate change and on behalf of climate justice.

- [**Diocese of
  Virginia**](https://episcopalvirginia.org/ministries/creation/)
  Concerned for the global climate emergency, drawing on diverse
  approaches for our diverse contexts, the Creation Care Committee
  commits to form and restore loving, liberating, life-giving
  relationships with all of Creation. The Committee focuses its work on
  four key areas of ministry: energy conservation, habitat restoration,
  policy and advocacy, and spiritual resilience.

- [**Diocese of Southern
  Ohio**](https://diosohio.org/new-resource-from-the-diocesan-commission-on-creation-care-and-environmental-justice/)
  The diocesan Commission on Creation Care and Environmental Justice (or
  CCEJ) convenes to support the leaders and faith communities of the
  Diocese of Southern Ohio for their efforts in caring for and seeking
  relationship with all God’s creation.

- [**Diocese of
  Olympia**](https://ecww.org/creation-care-climate-justice/) We are
  vested with the sacred duty (and immense pleasure) of caring for
  Creation. Creation needs us now. By pledging, our commitment becomes
  public and others will be inspired to join us. Pledging unites us in
  reflection and action through which we promise to study, understand,
  and renew our frayed relations with Creation and join with others to
  speak out on climate issues.

- [**Diocese of Western Oregon**](https://ecwo.org/creation-care/)
  Provide a contextual and fact-based scientific frame for understanding
  climate change for our diocese. Emphasis should be on the unique
  environmental and climate features of our diocese and the role of
  mitigation/adaptation. Include alignment with The Episcopal Church
  (TEC) Creation Care programs and events.
